scope: pre-submission review pass: two logged-out zero-context reviews + /proof read (the video third-party/PII audit component was completed 2026-08-26 against the export; see docs/submission/video-audit.md)
method: Two independent zero-context agents reviewed only public URLs from a logged-out perspective, with no credentials and no repository working copy. Reviewer 1 walked the judge product path (site, /proof, console, case pages, review-console refusal, video, social post). Reviewer 2 did cross-surface consistency (every shared number across README, Devpost copy, article, site, /proof, spike evidence), a full link check, a hygiene sweep, and article-vs-evidence spot checks. Every load-bearing finding was then re-verified directly by the controller before being recorded here.
surfaces_checked: https://github.com/sebastiancadena/keplaria (README, devpost.md, THIRD_PARTY.md, spike evidence via raw)
clean: All 23 checked links resolve logged-out; the review console 302s to accounts.google.com exactly as documented (x-goog-iap-generated-response header present)

Zero hard numeric contradictions across surfaces: 45.1 s, 22.4 s, 663.5 s, 19/20, 380 days, 130 s, 24/24, 629 tests, nine contracts, Gemma and Model Armor figures all agree cell for cell with their evidence files
No credentials, bearer tokens, signed URLs, personal emails, or undisclosed project identifiers on any public surface
The author-timed-not-practitioner-reviewed qualifier travels with the baseline on every surface
Article headline numbers verified against spikes/model_armor and spikes/gemini_37_eval evidence (full match; one labelled-manual historical figure, see findings)

findings.detail: At review time the X account limited post visibility: oembed refused and the syndication endpoint returned a TweetTombstone, so the bonus-content URL in the Devpost form was a dead end for judges. The user made the post public the same day; re-verified: syndication returns the Tweet (hashtag and article link intact) and oembed answers 200.

findings.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (fix deployed; freeze re-captured at eff56c0; the form carries no SHA, so no form edit was needed — devpost.md now points at the freeze evidence instead of quoting one)
findings.detail: On a rejected case (JR-A-C04699, REJ-B-564088) the lifecycle banner reads 'APPROVED - Released by a human at Ground Control' while the same page shows 'Human decision: rejected' and 'Effective band: blocked'. Verified in code: console/projection.py _status() returns APPROVED for any approval_id (a rejection included), and console/templates/case.html prints 'Released by a human' whenever a decision applies, never branching on the decision itself; the same template line's else branch makes finished clear-band cases read 'Awaiting a Ground Control decision'. approval.decision is already projected, so the fix is a small branch in each place.

The console's first group showed 21 cases under one supplier, ~20 near-identical JR-A-* rows awaiting approval (accumulated rehearsal runs), plus DLQ-SWEEP and DEMO-* probe rows, under a front page whose core sentence is 'one durable case per supplier'. Every live case id was mapped against every committed evidence file, the tracked tree, untracked files, the strategy repo, and the video repo's take logs: 27 cases are evidence-cited and must stay, 1 (JR-A-E98AC9) appears on camera in the video's Cloud Trace still, and the remaining 16 were cited nowhere. The user deleted those 16 via erp.py purge (dry-run inspected first); the store went 44 to 28, deleted pages 404, protected pages render, and the core-contracts harness re-proved 9/9 plus a clean erp.py audit afterwards. The rows that remain under one supplier are proof residue by design (the ten-run streak alone pins ten per supplier); accepted.

The example file labelled FRAPPE_API_KEY as 'admin-scoped owner keys' (it is the scoped executor) and omitted the FRAPPE_ADMIN_* owner pair entirely, contradicting the README's two-identity security claim on a file strangers are told to copy.

findings.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (user approved: all 28 evidence cells link to the file on GitHub, deployed and live-verified)
findings.detail: Every evidence cell on /proof is plain monospace text; the files are publicly reachable in the repo but the reader must reconstruct the URL by hand.

The article's 'dropped from 85 to 57 seconds' cites evidence that contains the 57 (56.9 s) but not the 85. The ledger row article_run_timing_at_publication is verify=manual with the reason recorded (published, historical, deliberately rounded; do not reconcile against today's number). A judge who follows the citation finds the label.

findings.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (user decision: MIT; LICENSE at root, THIRD_PARTY.md relicensing note)
findings.detail: GitHub shows no license; the disclosure lives inside THIRD_PARTY.md where a judge may not look first.

The caption and banner parts shipped with the console fix. What remains is accepted: REJ-B-564088's route label is a data quirk of that parked rehearsal case, not a rendering bug; 'DLQ' sits inside an immutable case id; and the site's 'parked' was checked and already carries an inline gloss at first use — the reviewer missed it.

verdicts.reviewer_1: The core product path survives the first ten minutes: every surface resolves logged-out, the refusal behaves as advertised, the cold read lands inside a minute, numbers agree everywhere. Worst issue was the invisible social post (since resolved); second, the rejected-case banner.
verdicts.reviewer_2: Zero hard numeric contradictions between surfaces, unusual for a hackathon submission; the claim-ledger architecture visibly works. Worst catch is the labelled-manual 85 figure; runners-up the missing LICENSE badge and the (now fixed) secrets-example mislabel.
